# OPmobility (OPM.PA) - Forensic Dossier (re-underwrite, 2026-10-12)

Live quote used throughout: EUR 9.46 on Euronext Paris (FMP, 12 October 2026, intraday; previous close EUR 9.725). The 52-week range is EUR 9.45 to EUR 18.16, so the stock is at its low. Primary sources: the first-half 2026 results call (22 July 2026, in the transcript file) and the 7 October 2026 guidance cut, reported in the French financial press (Boursorama, Abcbourse, Option Finance, Investing.com, 7 and 8 October 2026).

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Through 2025 and into mid-2026 management told a consistent story: a mature French car-parts maker (bumpers and exterior parts, lighting, fuel tanks, assembly modules) that keeps paying down debt whatever the car market does. In February 2026 it guided to higher operating profit, higher net income and free cash flow (the cash left after investment) of EUR 250-300 million, against 2025's EUR 490 million operating profit, EUR 185 million net income and EUR 297 million free cash flow. On 22 July 2026 it confirmed all of that, while admitting the market was running below its own plan.

On the evening of 7 October 2026 the story changed. Management cut the 2026 targets to an operating profit of EUR 430-450 million (down 8-12% on 2025 instead of up) and free cash flow "above EUR 220 million" (down about a quarter), dropped the promise of higher net income in favour of a "significant" one, and announced a European restructuring of about 770 jobs (460 in Germany, 310 in France) costing EUR 120-130 million this year. The reasons given were a weaker car market than expected (notably China), cost swings linked to Middle East tensions, cancelled hydrogen projects and weaker European customers. The one promise kept was that net debt will still be lower at end-2026 than at end-2025. The shares fell about 20% on 8 October, from EUR 12.44 to EUR 9.85, on roughly ten times normal volume.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- Data-feed error, carried from the prior record and still present: OPmobility reports half-yearly, and the feed files each half as a quarter, so the "trailing" figures in the screen add up two years. The supplied trailing earnings per share of EUR 2.49 is EUR 0.71 + 0.67 + 0.63 + 0.49; the true trailing figure is about EUR 1.37. The supplied trailing free cash flow of EUR 890 million is really about EUR 445 million. The screen's 3.1 times price-to-free-cash-flow is therefore wrong; on the new guidance (EUR 220 million) the shares trade at about 6.1 times this year's free cash flow, before restructuring cash is fully spent.
- Gross margin (sales less direct production costs) has fallen every year: 11.0% in 2023, 10.9% in 2024, 9.4% in 2025, and 9.6% in the first half of 2026 against 11.3% a year earlier. The October cut confirms what those numbers implied: the company cannot pass rising resin and energy costs on to carmakers.
- Return on invested capital (operating profit after tax divided by the money tied up in the business) peaked at about 7.0% in 2025 and was 6.4% for the year to June 2026; with operating profit now guided down about 10%, 2026 will be lower still - below any sensible cost of capital for a cyclical supplier with EUR 2.25 billion of gross debt.
- Balance sheet: at 30 June 2026, borrowings EUR 1.94 billion plus leases EUR 0.31 billion less cash EUR 0.815 billion = net debt EUR 1.43 billion including leases (about EUR 1.12 billion excluding leases). This file uses the lease-inclusive figure throughout. Debt has genuinely fallen two years running, and management still promises a lower figure at end-2026.
- First-half cash was flattered: EUR 423 million of operating cash flow included a EUR 97 million working-capital benefit from paying suppliers more slowly (EUR 335 million rise in payables), and the finance chief flagged lower factoring (selling receivables early) in the second half. The prior committee named this as the most likely disappointment; the October cut is it.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
February 2026: confident, "improvement" on every line. July 2026: still confirming, but the tone turned careful - the market assumption had gone from "more or less flat" to minus 2.3%, resin is unhedged, second-half cost recovery "really hard to anticipate", restructuring "not embedded in our figures". October 2026: retreat on profit and cash, defensive language ("financial discipline", "targeted competitiveness measures"). The trajectory is deteriorating, but the July hedges were honest warnings, which matters for how much to trust the new numbers.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Mixed and now damaged. The 2025 free-cash-flow and deleveraging targets were met. But the 2026 targets were confirmed on 22 July and cut eleven weeks later, and the restructuring that management said was not in its figures has now arrived at EUR 120-130 million. Deutsche Bank noted the new operating-profit midpoint is only about 1% below the analyst consensus it surveyed, meaning analysts had already marked down much of the miss; the free-cash-flow cut, and the restructuring cash, are the genuine news. The credibility test is now whether the reduced EUR 220 million free cash flow and the lower year-end net debt are delivered at the full-year results (late February 2027).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
July call: analysts pressed on the second-half cash bridge (payables reversal, less factoring), on the undisclosed price and financing of the Hyundai Mobis lighting acquisition ("all of the figures that we are disclosing are without anything linked to this project"), and on the European Industrial Accelerator Act (CEO: "Unfortunately, not" on any timetable). October: Deutsche Bank cut its target from EUR 14 to EUR 11 (neutral stance kept); Oddo BHF cut from EUR 21 to EUR 15 and called the message a negative signal for European suppliers in general, since the causes are sector-wide (cost pressure, inability to pass on inflation, overcapacity, weak volumes).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Red: guidance cut eleven weeks after reconfirmation; gross margin down four years in five; returns below cost of capital and falling; cancelled hydrogen projects remove part of the long-term "beyond the combustion engine" story; an acquisition still unpriced; equity is a thin slice of the enterprise (net debt is about the same size as the market value), so every 1% move in operating earnings moves the equity about 2%.
Green: net-debt reduction for 2026 reaffirmed; free cash flow still positive and guided above EUR 220 million after restructuring; fuel-tank global share rising (21% to 23%, aim 30% by 2030) in a consolidating niche; family control (Burelle, about 63% of shares) rules out forced selling of the majority of the register; the restructuring is a cost cut, which should help 2027-28 margins.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- The 8 October fall dragged other European suppliers down the same day (Option Finance: "entraine le secteur dans son sillage"), so part of the move is a sector-wide re-pricing rather than a pure single-name event - but the trigger was this company's own announcement.
- Hydrogen-mobility project cancellations are a quiet admission that one leg of the long-term transition story is slipping; the fuel-tank franchise remains the profit engine, and its base shrinks as battery cars gain share.
- Dividends paid fell from EUR 54 million in H1 2025 to EUR 43 million in H1 2026; with net income no longer guided up, the 2027 payout is at risk, which could push out income-focused holders.
- Free float is only about 37% of shares (about EUR 500 million at today's price), so liquidity is thin and moves overshoot both ways.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
A competent, honest-enough management running a structurally low-return business in a bad cycle. The deleveraging discipline is real and still promised; the earnings power is lower than the market believed in July, and the pricing-power problem is now confirmed rather than suspected. The price has fallen a long way, but so has the fair value. Treat the next hard read - full-year 2026 results in late February 2027, where the EUR 220 million cash figure and the lower net debt are either delivered or not - as the proof point before committing capital.

# OPmobility (OPM.PA) - Forensic Dossier (re-underwrite, 2026-10-12)

Live quote used throughout: EUR 9.46 on Euronext Paris (FMP, 12 October 2026, intraday; previous close EUR 9.725). The 52-week range is EUR 9.45 to EUR 18.16, so the stock is at its low. Primary sources: the first-half 2026 results call (22 July 2026, in the transcript file) and the 7 October 2026 guidance cut, reported in the French financial press (Boursorama, Abcbourse, Option Finance, Investing.com, 7 and 8 October 2026).

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Through 2025 and into mid-2026 management told a consistent story: a mature French car-parts maker (bumpers and exterior parts, lighting, fuel tanks, assembly modules) that keeps paying down debt whatever the car market does. In February 2026 it guided to higher operating profit, higher net income and free cash flow (the cash left after investment) of EUR 250-300 million, against 2025's EUR 490 million operating profit, EUR 185 million net income and EUR 297 million free cash flow. On 22 July 2026 it confirmed all of that, while admitting the market was running below its own plan.

On the evening of 7 October 2026 the story changed. Management cut the 2026 targets to an operating profit of EUR 430-450 million (down 8-12% on 2025 instead of up) and free cash flow "above EUR 220 million" (down about a quarter), dropped the promise of higher net income in favour of a "significant" one, and announced a European restructuring of about 770 jobs (460 in Germany, 310 in France) costing EUR 120-130 million this year. The reasons given were a weaker car market than expected (notably China), cost swings linked to Middle East tensions, cancelled hydrogen projects and weaker European customers. The one promise kept was that net debt will still be lower at end-2026 than at end-2025. The shares fell about 20% on 8 October, from EUR 12.44 to EUR 9.85, on roughly ten times normal volume.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- Data-feed error, carried from the prior record and still present: OPmobility reports half-yearly, and the feed files each half as a quarter, so the "trailing" figures in the screen add up two years. The supplied trailing earnings per share of EUR 2.49 is EUR 0.71 + 0.67 + 0.63 + 0.49; the true trailing figure is about EUR 1.37. The supplied trailing free cash flow of EUR 890 million is really about EUR 445 million. The screen's 3.1 times price-to-free-cash-flow is therefore wrong; on the new guidance (EUR 220 million) the shares trade at about 6.1 times this year's free cash flow, before restructuring cash is fully spent.
- Gross margin (sales less direct production costs) has fallen every year: 11.0% in 2023, 10.9% in 2024, 9.4% in 2025, and 9.6% in the first half of 2026 against 11.3% a year earlier. The October cut confirms what those numbers implied: the company cannot pass rising resin and energy costs on to carmakers.
- Return on invested capital (operating profit after tax divided by the money tied up in the business) peaked at about 7.0% in 2025 and was 6.4% for the year to June 2026; with operating profit now guided down about 10%, 2026 will be lower still - below any sensible cost of capital for a cyclical supplier with EUR 2.25 billion of gross debt.
- Balance sheet: at 30 June 2026, borrowings EUR 1.94 billion plus leases EUR 0.31 billion less cash EUR 0.815 billion = net debt EUR 1.43 billion including leases (about EUR 1.12 billion excluding leases). This file uses the lease-inclusive figure throughout. Debt has genuinely fallen two years running, and management still promises a lower figure at end-2026.
- First-half cash was flattered: EUR 423 million of operating cash flow included a EUR 97 million working-capital benefit from paying suppliers more slowly (EUR 335 million rise in payables), and the finance chief flagged lower factoring (selling receivables early) in the second half. The prior committee named this as the most likely disappointment; the October cut is it.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
February 2026: confident, "improvement" on every line. July 2026: still confirming, but the tone turned careful - the market assumption had gone from "more or less flat" to minus 2.3%, resin is unhedged, second-half cost recovery "really hard to anticipate", restructuring "not embedded in our figures". October 2026: retreat on profit and cash, defensive language ("financial discipline", "targeted competitiveness measures"). The trajectory is deteriorating, but the July hedges were honest warnings, which matters for how much to trust the new numbers.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Mixed and now damaged. The 2025 free-cash-flow and deleveraging targets were met. But the 2026 targets were confirmed on 22 July and cut eleven weeks later, and the restructuring that management said was not in its figures has now arrived at EUR 120-130 million. Deutsche Bank noted the new operating-profit midpoint is only about 1% below the analyst consensus it surveyed, meaning analysts had already marked down much of the miss; the free-cash-flow cut, and the restructuring cash, are the genuine news. The credibility test is now whether the reduced EUR 220 million free cash flow and the lower year-end net debt are delivered at the full-year results (late February 2027).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
July call: analysts pressed on the second-half cash bridge (payables reversal, less factoring), on the undisclosed price and financing of the Hyundai Mobis lighting acquisition ("all of the figures that we are disclosing are without anything linked to this project"), and on the European Industrial Accelerator Act (CEO: "Unfortunately, not" on any timetable). October: Deutsche Bank cut its target from EUR 14 to EUR 11 (neutral stance kept); Oddo BHF cut from EUR 21 to EUR 15 and called the message a negative signal for European suppliers in general, since the causes are sector-wide (cost pressure, inability to pass on inflation, overcapacity, weak volumes).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Red: guidance cut eleven weeks after reconfirmation; gross margin down four years in five; returns below cost of capital and falling; cancelled hydrogen projects remove part of the long-term "beyond the combustion engine" story; an acquisition still unpriced; equity is a thin slice of the enterprise (net debt is about the same size as the market value), so every 1% move in operating earnings moves the equity about 2%.
Green: net-debt reduction for 2026 reaffirmed; free cash flow still positive and guided above EUR 220 million after restructuring; fuel-tank global share rising (21% to 23%, aim 30% by 2030) in a consolidating niche; family control (Burelle, about 63% of shares) rules out forced selling of the majority of the register; the restructuring is a cost cut, which should help 2027-28 margins.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- The 8 October fall dragged other European suppliers down the same day (Option Finance: "entraine le secteur dans son sillage"), so part of the move is a sector-wide re-pricing rather than a pure single-name event - but the trigger was this company's own announcement.
- Hydrogen-mobility project cancellations are a quiet admission that one leg of the long-term transition story is slipping; the fuel-tank franchise remains the profit engine, and its base shrinks as battery cars gain share.
- Dividends paid fell from EUR 54 million in H1 2025 to EUR 43 million in H1 2026; with net income no longer guided up, the 2027 payout is at risk, which could push out income-focused holders.
- Free float is only about 37% of shares (about EUR 500 million at today's price), so liquidity is thin and moves overshoot both ways.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
A competent, honest-enough management running a structurally low-return business in a bad cycle. The deleveraging discipline is real and still promised; the earnings power is lower than the market believed in July, and the pricing-power problem is now confirmed rather than suspected. The price has fallen a long way, but so has the fair value. Treat the next hard read - full-year 2026 results in late February 2027, where the EUR 220 million cash figure and the lower net debt are either delivered or not - as the proof point before committing capital.

bull_thesis:
OPmobility, the renamed Plastic Omnium, is a family-controlled French car-parts maker whose shares, at EUR 9.62 on the Paris market (live quote, 10 November 2026), sit about 7% above a 52-week low after halving from EUR 18.16. The bullish case is that the 7 October guidance cut reset expectations to a level the business can beat, and the 21 October revenue release is the first sign it is holding that line.

First, the top line has stabilised. Third-quarter revenue rose 2.8% like-for-like to EUR 2,437 million, with Europe up 8.6% and the rest of Asia up 12.3%, and management confirmed every reduced target on 21 October, two weeks after cutting them.

Second, deleveraging survives. Net debt including leases was EUR 1.43 billion at 30 June 2026 and is promised lower at end-2026 even after EUR 120-130 million of restructuring. Free cash flow above EUR 220 million is about 16% of today's EUR 1.38 billion market value.

Third, self-help and consolidation. The 770-job European restructuring should save something like EUR 50-60 million a year from 2027-28; the fuel-tank franchise is gaining share (21% to 23%, aim 30% by 2030); and the Hyundai Mobis lighting business is being bought for about EUR 390 million, roughly 0.24 times its EUR 1.6 billion of sales, which could add scale cheaply if its margin holds.
bear_thesis:
The bearish case is that the guidance cut confirmed the structural problem the numbers had been signalling for two years, and that the stock is still not cheap against its nearest peers.

First, pricing power is absent. Gross margin (sales less direct production costs) fell from 11.0% in 2023 to 10.9% in 2024, 9.4% in 2025 and 9.6% in the first half of 2026 against 11.3% a year earlier. On 22 July management called second-half resin cost recovery from customers 'really hard to anticipate'; on 7 October it cited cost swings and weaker customers. Oddo BHF read the cut as sector-wide: cost pressure, inability to pass on inflation, overcapacity and weak volumes.

Second, returns sit below the cost of capital and are falling. Return on invested capital peaked near 7.0% in 2025, was 6.4% in the year to June 2026, and an operating profit guided down about 10% takes it lower again. A business earning less than its capital costs does not deserve a premium multiple.

Third, credibility took a hit. The 2026 targets were confirmed on 22 July and cut eleven weeks later; the restructuring management said was 'not embedded in our figures' has arrived. The Hyundai Mobis lighting acquisition is still unpriced and unfinanced in public, and the hydrogen projects that were part of the long-term story are being cancelled.

Fourth, leverage magnifies everything. Net debt of EUR 1.43 billion is about the same size as the EUR 1.35 billion market value, so each 1% change in operating earnings moves the equity value by roughly 2%. At EUR 9.46 the enterprise value (market value plus net debt) is about EUR 2.82 billion, or about 3.3 times the roughly EUR 850 million of operating cash earnings (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) the new guidance implies - still above Valeo and Forvia at about 2.4 and 2.7 times when last struck on 31 August, before the sector fell further on 8 October. And the screen's 'deep value' flag rests partly on a data error: the feed adds two years of half-yearly results into one 'trailing' year, doubling earnings per share (EUR 2.49 supplied versus about EUR 1.37 true) and free cash flow.
consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market is small. At about 3.3 times this year's operating cash earnings and about 6 times guided free cash flow the stock looks cheap until set against Valeo and Forvia, which trade lower still. We agree with the market's doubt about the margin story: four years of falling gross margin and the October cut show the company cannot pass on input costs. Where we may differ is on cash discipline: management kept the net-debt promise through the cut and reconfirmed it on 21 October, and if EUR 220 million of free cash flow and lower year-end debt are delivered in February the stock could re-rate toward our EUR 11.15 base case. That is a wager on proof that has not arrived, and the newly priced EUR 390 million Hyundai Mobis deal means 2027 debt will rise again on completion.
forcing_function: The one dated event that settles the question is the full-year 2026 results, expected late February 2027 (the prior year's came on 25 February 2026), when the reduced free cash flow, year-end net debt, restructuring cash and 2027 outlook are reported together. The 21 October revenue release has passed without testing cash. Completion of the Hyundai Mobis lighting deal (second half of 2027) and the European Industrial Accelerator Act have no binding dates.
valley_of_death: The risky window (the period when the thesis is most exposed before it can be proven) runs from now to the full-year results in late February 2027. Four hazards sit inside it. First, the second-half cash bridge: H1 operating cash flow was flattered by EUR 97 million of slower supplier payments that tend to reverse, and factoring (selling receivables early) is being reduced, so even the lowered EUR 220 million needs a decent second half. Second, the restructuring cash: EUR 120-130 million of charges this year, some of which will be paid in 2027. Third, the Hyundai Mobis lighting acquisition: if it is priced and debt-funded inside this window it could push leverage back up just as the deleveraging story is all that is left. Fourth, European carmakers - Renault, Stellantis and Volkswagen were all named by analysts in October - are cutting production schedules, which could force a second cut. The dividend, already lower in H1 2026, could also be trimmed at the February results.
positioning_washout: This was not a wash-out (a sharp sell-off by forced or non-fundamental sellers). The 8 October fall came from company news - the 7 October guidance cut - and was amplified by a same-day sell-off across European car-parts suppliers. About 63% of the shares are held by the Burelle family and cannot be forced out, so the thin free float (about EUR 500 million) moves violently on news but has no mechanical seller behind it. Remaining sellers are income funds if the dividend is cut in February and holders who bought the deleveraging story and now see free cash flow down a quarter. Neither is a dated, forced event to wait for.
moderator_conclusion:
Wait for proof: we buy once the full-year 2026 results show free cash flow of at least EUR 220 million and net debt below end-2025, due late February 2027.

Nothing since our 12 October debate changes that answer. On 21 October the company reported third-quarter revenue up 2.8% like-for-like and confirmed the targets it had cut two weeks earlier, which is what it needed to say but not yet proof: cash flow and debt are only reported with the full-year results. The thesis is in doubt until then. The same release priced the Hyundai Mobis lighting deal at about EUR 390 million, to close in the second half of 2027; we treat it as roughly value-neutral, but it will lift debt again after the year-end test.

At EUR 9.62 our base-case value of about EUR 11.15 a share is roughly 16% above the price - short of the 20% margin we require in today's environment of growth with sticky inflation - against an adverse case near EUR 5.15, and the stock is still priced above Valeo and Forvia on enterprise value to operating cash earnings. Conviction stays at 2: a low-return, leveraged supplier with falling margins, where the only clean support is the cash-and-debt promise we are waiting to see kept.
sop_fair_value: EUR 11.15 per share (range EUR 10.50 to EUR 12.50)
sop_breakdown: Base case on about EUR 850 million of operating cash earnings, which is what the new 2026 operating-profit midpoint of EUR 440 million plus roughly EUR 410 million of depreciation implies, held flat into 2027 as restructuring savings offset a soft market. Multiples are cut from the prior base to reflect the confirmed absence of pricing power. Powertrain, mostly fuel tanks: EUR 290 million at 4.5 times = EUR 1.31 billion. Exterior and Lighting: EUR 380 million at 2.8 times = EUR 1.06 billion. Modules: EUR 180 million at 2.5 times = EUR 0.45 billion. Joint ventures at three-quarters of carrying value: EUR 0.30 billion. Gross value EUR 3.12 billion; less net debt of EUR 1.433 billion including leases (lease-inclusive to match the lease-inclusive earnings measure; about EUR 1.12 billion excluding leases), about EUR 60 million of restructuring cash still to be paid in 2027, and EUR 32 million of minorities = equity EUR 1.59 billion on 142.9 million shares = EUR 11.15. The implied blended multiple is about 3.3 times operating cash earnings - still a premium of roughly 20-35% to Valeo and Forvia, which the committee allows only for the fuel-tank franchise and the deleveraging record. Cross-check: on about EUR 1.10 of normalised earnings per share (after restructuring), EUR 11.15 is about 10 times earnings, in line with where European tier-one suppliers have historically traded mid-cycle. Update 2026-11-10: the Hyundai Mobis lighting deal (enterprise value about EUR 390 million, completion second half of 2027) is treated as value-neutral - bought for debt at roughly what it is worth - so it adds neither parts value nor a deduction to the base case.
risk_reward: At EUR 9.62 the base case of EUR 11.15 sits about EUR 1.55 above the price and the adverse case of EUR 5.15 about EUR 4.45 below it; the favourable case of EUR 16.50 needs both a European production recovery and full restructuring savings. The downside remains larger than the central upside because the equity is a thin slice on top of EUR 1.43 billion of net debt. The pipeline computes the ratios from these levels.
catalyst_status_plain: a soft catalyst, no fixed date
peer_comps_note: The peer file (Forvia, Valeo, Magna, Martinrea, Autoneum, Gestamp, Continental) calls OPmobility cheap, but that verdict rests on the 3.0 times price-to-free-cash-flow figure, which inherits the feed's doubling of half-yearly results; the true figure is about 6.2 times guided 2026 free cash flow. On enterprise value (about EUR 2.8 billion at EUR 9.62) to the roughly EUR 850 million of operating cash earnings implied by the new guidance, OPmobility is about 3.3 times, above Valeo and Forvia (about 2.4 and 2.7 times when last struck on 2026-08-31, both lower since the sector sell-off of 2026-10-08). Magna and Martinrea are North American and Continental is electronics-led, so they are weaker anchors. Part of the October de-rating was shared across European suppliers (Oddo BHF called the causes sector-wide), so any discount to the committee's old fair value is partly sector beta rather than name-specific edge. Verdict: rich against the two closest French peers.
interrogator_dossier:
# OPmobility (OPM.PA) - Forensic Dossier (continuing coverage, 2026-11-10)

Live quote used throughout: EUR 9.62 on Euronext Paris (FMP, 10 November 2026; previous close EUR 9.51). The 52-week range is EUR 9.01 to EUR 18.16, so the stock sits about 7% above its low and well below its 50-day (EUR 10.89) and 200-day (EUR 13.78) averages. Primary sources: the full-year 2025 call (25 February 2026) and first-half 2026 call (22 July 2026) in the transcript file; the 7 October 2026 guidance cut (French financial press); and the third-quarter 2026 revenue release of 21 October 2026 (reported by Ideal Investisseur and Reuters syndication). This file updates the committee's 12 October 2026 dossier; the only new company disclosure since then is the 21 October revenue release.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Through 2025 and into mid-2026 management told a consistent story: a mature French car-parts maker (bumpers and exterior parts, lighting, fuel tanks, assembly modules) that keeps paying down debt whatever the car market does. On 7 October 2026 that story was cut back: 2026 operating profit guided to EUR 430-450 million (from an improvement on 2025's EUR 490 million), free cash flow (the cash left after investment) to "above EUR 220 million" (from EUR 250-300 million), and a European restructuring of about 770 jobs costing EUR 120-130 million. The shares fell about 20% on 8 October.

On 21 October 2026 management reported third-quarter revenue of EUR 2,437 million, up 2.8% on a like-for-like basis (same scope, constant currency), and confirmed every one of the lowered targets, including lower net debt at end-2026 than at end-2025. Nine-month revenue was EUR 7,639 million, up 1.1% like-for-like. The narrative is now one of holding the reduced line rather than recovering it.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- Data-feed error, still present: OPmobility reports half-yearly and the feed files each half as a quarter, so the supplied trailing figures double-count. The trailing earnings per share of EUR 2.49 is really about EUR 1.37, and the trailing free cash flow of EUR 890 million is really about EUR 445 million. The screen's 3.0 times price-to-free-cash-flow is wrong; on the EUR 220 million guidance the shares trade at about 6.2 times this year's free cash flow at a EUR 1.38 billion market value.
- Gross margin (sales less direct production costs) has fallen every year: 11.0% in 2023, 10.9% in 2024, 9.4% in 2025, 9.6% in the first half of 2026 against 11.3% a year earlier. Pricing power is the weak point and nothing in the October revenue release addresses it (it carries no margin data).
- Third-quarter mix: Exterior and Lighting EUR 1,081 million (+4.1% like-for-like), Modules EUR 721 million (+3.2%), Powertrain EUR 635 million (+0.5%). Europe rose 8.6% like-for-like, led by Eastern Europe; North America fell 5.9% reported; China economic revenue (including joint ventures) fell 33.2% like-for-like to EUR 195 million, and joint-venture sales fell 19.0%. The consolidated top line is holding; the equity-accounted China income behind it is shrinking fast.
- Return on invested capital peaked near 7.0% in 2025 and was 6.4% for the year to June 2026; with operating profit guided down about 10%, 2026 will be lower - below a sensible cost of capital for a leveraged cyclical.
- Balance sheet at 30 June 2026: borrowings EUR 1.94 billion plus leases EUR 0.31 billion less cash EUR 0.815 billion = net debt EUR 1.43 billion including leases (about EUR 1.12 billion excluding leases). This file uses the lease-inclusive figure.
- Hyundai Mobis lighting acquisition, now priced: enterprise value 600 billion won (about EUR 390 million at the 29 September 2026 rate) for a business with about EUR 1.6 billion of 2025 revenue and a positive operating margin, completion targeted for the second half of 2027 subject to approvals. Management says it should not significantly affect deleveraging. At about 0.24 times sales it is not expensive, but it is roughly a quarter of today's net debt added on completion, and the margin of the acquired business is not disclosed.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
February 2026: confident, "improvement" on every line. July 2026: careful - resin unhedged, second-half cost recovery "really hard to anticipate", restructuring "not embedded in our figures". October 7: retreat on profit and cash. October 21: steady, factual confirmation of the reduced targets with a positive like-for-like quarter. The slide in tone has stopped for now, but there is no sign of a rebuild.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Damaged and not yet repaired. The 2025 free-cash-flow and deleveraging targets were met, but the 2026 targets were confirmed on 22 July and cut eleven weeks later. The 21 October reconfirmation is two weeks after the cut and carries little information about cash: the free-cash-flow and net-debt figures are only tested at the full-year results, expected late February 2027 (the prior year's were published 25 February 2026).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
July call: the second-half cash bridge (EUR 97 million of slower supplier payments that tend to reverse, less factoring - selling receivables early), the then-unpriced Hyundai Mobis deal, and the European Industrial Accelerator Act (no timetable). October: Deutsche Bank cut its target from EUR 14 to EUR 11; Oddo BHF from EUR 21 to EUR 15, calling the causes sector-wide. No newer dated target changes were found for November.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Red: guidance cut eleven weeks after reconfirmation; gross margin down four years in five; returns below cost of capital; China joint-venture revenue down a third; a EUR 390 million acquisition to be paid in 2027 on a balance sheet whose net debt roughly equals the market value; hydrogen projects cancelled.
Green: reduced targets reconfirmed on 21 October with a positive like-for-like quarter; Europe growing 8.6%; net debt promised lower at end-2026; fuel-tank global share rising (21% to 23%, aim 30% by 2030); Burelle family control (about 63%) rules out forced selling of most of the register; restructuring savings should help 2027-28.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- The fall in China joint-venture income will not show in consolidated revenue but does reduce equity-accounted profit and dividends up from the joint ventures, which feed net income and cash.
- The Hyundai Mobis deal doubles the lighting exposure, a segment that has struggled with launch costs; it is a bet on scale in a low-margin line, priced cheaply for a reason.
- Free float is about 37% of shares (about EUR 510 million at today's price), so moves overshoot both ways on thin news.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
A competent, honest-enough management running a structurally low-return, leveraged business in a weak cycle. Nothing since 12 October changes the committee's read: the 21 October release confirmed the reduced targets but cannot test them, and the newly priced Hyundai Mobis deal adds about EUR 390 million of commitments in 2027. The proof point is unchanged - full-year 2026 results in late February 2027, where the EUR 220 million free cash flow and the lower net debt are delivered or not.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening.
thesis_evidence: The load-bearing claim - that free cash flow and falling debt carry the equity through a weak car market - is in doubt but not disproven. On 2026-10-07 management cut 2026 free cash flow to above EUR 220 million (from EUR 250-300 million) and operating profit to EUR 430-450 million, adding EUR 120-130 million of restructuring. On 2026-10-21 it confirmed those reduced targets and lower year-end net debt alongside third-quarter revenue up 2.8% like-for-like, but disclosed no cash or debt figures, so the test is unchanged. Gross margin of 9.6% in H1 2026 against 11.3% a year earlier (H1 report, 2026-07-22) still confirms weak pricing power, and China joint-venture revenue fell 33% like-for-like in the third quarter. The price has moved only from EUR 9.46 to EUR 9.62 since the last debate; there has been no wash-out (a sharp sell-off by forced or non-fundamental sellers) since then.
